sim.heading: Berry render simulator
faas.typeservice.ready: Type checking against the ctx/cap contract is active.
faas.typeservice.unavailable: Type checking unavailable — the editor stays fully usable.
sim.subtitle: Runs the real pinned Berry VM + the real fb.c in your browser — the frame is byte-identical to the device's. A separate surface from the C2 command editor above: here fb.* drawing calls are the point. On-device stays authoritative.
sim.no_frame: Press Run to render the current script.
sim.error_deadline: Aborted: exceeded the 100 ms simulator budget
sim.unavailable_body: The Berry-WASM module did not load (it is a build product of firmware/sim/build.sh, embedded at deploy). The editor above stays fully functional — lint, autocomplete and examples all work; only live rendering is unavailable.
sim.boundary_heading: What this does and does not simulate
sim.boundary_body: Simulated: the real VM drawing real pixels under the scenario values below. NOT simulated: NVS persistence across wakes, the RTC / wall-clock time, the network, timing and e-ink ghosting. The frame reflects only the path taken under these scenario values — not every reachable effect.
sim.pin_unbuilt: VM provenance: built at deploy (run firmware/sim/build.sh to see the pin here).
sim.c2.heading: Effect trace (illustrative)
sim.c2.subtitle: What this C2 script does when run against the stubbed device state below.
sim.c2.s8_label: Static analysis beats the trace. Severing warnings come only from the static lint above — never from this run: a call hidden behind a branch that is false in the simulator can still be true on-device.
sim.c2.empty: No C2 calls in this script yet.
sim.c2.failed: rejected — wrong argument type (a silent no-op on-device)
sim.c2.boundary: This trace shows only the path taken under the device state above — not every reachable effect.
sim.effect.set_url: Sets the C2 poll URL to “{url}” — points the device at a new server.

sim.effect.net_clear: Clears the cached network config — the device drops its current connection (severing).
sim.effect.tx_power: Sets the Wi-Fi transmit power to {dbm} dBm.
sim.effect.reboot: Reboots the device after this poll finishes.
sim.effect.refresh: Forces a frame refresh on the device.
sim.effect.device_sleep: Puts the device into deep sleep for {s} seconds.

berry.title: Berry
berry.intro: Author a C2 command script. Lint and autocomplete are best-effort, client-side, pre-flight — the authoritative compile check is on-device, and its result never returns (the cursor advances either way). Enqueue ships in a later wave.
berry.starter: # Author a Berry C2 command. Autocomplete offers the safe subset only.
berry.caps_sub: the C2 safe subset — autocomplete offers exactly these.
berry.severing_title: can cut the device's own C2 path
berry.fleet_warn: ⚠ broadcast to {devices}. The queue is append-only — there is no recall. A device onboarded later will not receive it (its cursor seeds past this command).
berry.arm_aria: type asterisk to arm the fleet broadcast
berry.risk_fleet_severing: ⚠ HIGHEST RISK — a fleet-wide severing command can strand the WHOLE fleet at once (USB recovery only). It is allowed, but there is no recall.
berry.risk_severing: ⚠ this script calls a severing capability — it can cut the device's own C2 path (USB recovery only).
berry.note_ph: operator label (lands in the audit trail)
berry.enqueued: enqueued seq {seq} → {where} (delivered on the device's next poll)
berry.feedback_note: Cursor-advance only. “applied” means delivered + attempted — not proof the script ran: the device persists the ack even if the script faulted, and there is no device→server result channel. The device log is the only place the real outcome may surface.
berry.lint.severing: {name}() is severing — it can cut the device's own C2 path (USB recovery only).
berry.lint.forbidden: {name}() is a {phase} capability — not in the C2 executor; it faults at runtime and the cursor still advances (no error surfaced).
berry.lint.unknown_suggest: {name}() is not a C2 capability — did you mean {hint}()?

faas.intro: Author render / schedule / webhook functions for the FaaS engine. Edit the source, configure the trigger / egress / secret bindings / dither, and enable when ready. Test-run + frame preview arrive in the next wave — this surface authors, it does not execute.
